name: Lab 4.2 - Counter Reset Lamp
description: Count raw operator pulses in the PLC counter, light the lamp at its preset, and clear the count with a momentary reset.

hints: Count rising edges of pulse_received with a PLC CTU. The reference preset is three, inherited from the preceding example.
reset_pressed clears the counter; it takes priority if count and reset arrive in the same scan. Both buttons produce one accepted-scan pulse.
The controller owns the counter and counter_lamp. The default exercise has no loaded solution; author or explicitly open a controller before Run.

solution.summary: This is an original functional reference for the control concept, not a copy of the photographed solution.
steps: Count raw pulse_received edges with a CTU; inhibit counting while reset_pressed is true.
Reset the CTU from reset_pressed before evaluating its done bit for counter_lamp.
Stop removes the output but retains the count; application Reset clears the complete controller and stops it.
solution.acceptance: Three separate count pulses light the reference lamp; reset clears count and lamp, and a subsequent new count starts at one.

machineGuide.purpose: Count raw operator pulses in the PLC counter, light the lamp at its preset, and clear the count with a momentary reset.
startConditions: The common PLC/watchdog foundation is healthy.
All required simulator inputs are at their documented initial state.
normalSequence: Author or explicitly load a compatible counter/reset ladder project and Run.
Press COUNT three times, waiting for the input to return false between presses.
Press RESET to clear the counter and lamp; the next COUNT starts a new batch.
stopBehavior: Stop clears lamp command and unscanned momentary inputs while retaining the accumulated PLC count.
Run resumes the counter; application Reset clears all inputs, outputs and counter state and stays stopped.
faultBehavior: A missing or stale input must fail safe and remain diagnosable.
expectedObservations: Three separate count pulses light the reference lamp; reset clears count and lamp, and a subsequent new count starts at one.

changedTags: count_reached removed: use raw pulse_received; the PLC owns accumulated count/done state.
